source_name: CBCG - Izvještaj o stabilnosti finansijskog sistema (Financial Stability Report)
why_relevant: Supervisory-analytical counterpart to Big-4/IFI assessments; sections on payment systems, digitalisation and operational/cyber risk describe infrastructure programmes and their state of play, providing the domestic baseline against which EC/IMF/EBRD statements can be triangulated.

source_name: CBCG — Pravila platnog sistema CBCG (payment system rules PDF)
why_relevant: The binding operating rules of the national payment system: participation criteria (personnel, organisational, technical), connectivity/technical requirements, message standards and settlement windows. Technical annexes of such rules are where interface specs, certification obligations and implicitly the platform's technology are revealed.

source_name: CBCG — RTGS sistem participant/agent registry PDF
why_relevant: Structured register entry for the RTGS system itself (operator, legal basis, participants). Machine-friendly, low-volume, high-signal artefact for tracking who is connected to national settlement.

entity_name: Uprava za javne nabavke / Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki
source_name: Državna komisija za kontrolu postupaka javnih nabavki — izvještaj o radu (gov.me document store)
why_relevant: Annual work reports aggregate appeal statistics and frequently cite illustrative cases with contracting authority and subject matter; helps size how many IT/banking-equipment tenders are contested and identify serial appellants (often the losing vendor).

entity_name: Uprava za javne nabavke / Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki
source_name: Government of Montenegro - Platforma ekonomskog oporavka 2022-2026 and successor reform programmes
why_relevant: National recovery/reform platforms set out digitalisation and financial-infrastructure measures with budgets and responsible institutions; these are the programme documents that IFI assessments then score, and they precede tenders.

entity_name: Uprava za javne nabavke / Direktorat za politiku javnih nabavki
source_name: Ministarstvo finansija Crne Gore - Direktorat za ekonomsku politiku, banking sector analyses
why_relevant: Ministry of Finance economic-policy directorate bulletins quantify banking-sector performance and reference reform/modernisation programmes; they are the government-side counterpart that EC and IMF assessments draw on and often cite adviser-produced studies.

source_name: Bankar.me — conference / event coverage (Infintech, IT Spot, Tomorrow)
why_relevant: Conference write-ups enumerate the actor map: which local IT companies serve banks (e.g. Logate, organiser of Infintech, run by Ivica Tatar), which banks send speakers, and which fintech topics are commercially live. Strong snowball seed into vendor websites and sponsor lists.

source_name: CFO Asocijacija Crne Gore (Association of Financial Directors) — newly formed
why_relevant: Newly constituted national CFO association (AMM initiative) — a forming buyer community for treasury, payments and finance-automation vendors. Currently only traceable through press coverage; watch for an own domain and member roster.

entity_name: World Bank STEP-derived Procurement Contract Awards datasets
source_name: World Bank ECA regional brief — Western Balkans Payment Modernization / SEPA programme
why_relevant: Programme-level narrative that explains the EU–World Bank–RCC architecture behind Montenegro's October 2025 SEPA accession and the instant-payments roadmap; sets the sequencing of national procurements that follow.

entity_name: World Bank STEP-derived Procurement Contract Awards datasets
source_name: World Bank — Montenegro FSAP Technical Note (payments and settlements infrastructure)
why_relevant: Independent assessment describing the actual architecture: CBCG-owned RTGS+DNS as the only interbank infrastructure, the Central Depository Agency as CSD, and an interoperable ATM/POS network whose routing and settlement runs over the international card scheme networks (i.e. no domestic card switch). This is the best single authoritative statement of the ME infrastructure baseline, and the World Bank is also a named supporter of the TIPS Clone project.

entity_name: World Bank STEP-derived Procurement Contract Awards datasets
source_name: World Bank - Montenegro digital financial services / digital payments modernisation project
why_relevant: An EUR 8m World Bank loan to modernise Montenegro's digital payments infrastructure. IFI project documents (PAD, procurement plans, ISR) name components, implementing agencies and eventually awarded contractors - the most direct public route to identifying competitor vendors on a national payments programme.

source_name: CKB consolidated audited financial statements (IFRS notes) - PDF
why_relevant: Audited annual statements of ME banks carry 'nematerijalna ulaganja / softver' (intangibles/software) notes, capex on IT, and sometimes operating-lease or service-contract disclosures that indirectly size IT spend and occasionally name suppliers. For privately-held systemic banks with no public procurement, this is one of very few quantitative windows onto technology investment.

source_name: Glasnik Privredne komore Crne Gore (chamber bulletin, PDF)
why_relevant: Monthly/periodic chamber bulletin reporting board sessions, member-company presentations, delegations and signed cooperation agreements — surfaces vendor-bank interactions that never reach the general press.

source_name: Erste Bank Montenegro - e-banking platform migration notices (vendor-revealing bank page)
why_relevant: Bank-side customer notices are a reliable indirect confirmation of vendor switches: this page documents Erste ME migrating corporate e-banking from the Halcom platform to Asseco/ASEE eMon OfficeBanking. Bank notice pages date the change, which vendor marketing pages usually do not.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — 'E-services and digital infrastructure as a response to COVID-19' (EU-funded, with MJU)
why_relevant: Donor-implemented digital projects publish results, partner and often contractor names that the ministry itself omits. UNDP procurement notices for these projects are a second, parallel channel naming e-service/e-payment implementers.

source_name: UNDP Montenegro — FinTech regulatory framework assessment (regional/donor analysis)
why_relevant: Donor-funded assessments name incumbent providers, market structure and cross-border dependencies that vendors do not publish; they also list stakeholders consulted, which functions as an actor map for the ME fintech/banking supply side.

entity_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore
source_name: Komisija za tržište kapitala Crne Gore (SCMN) — "Montenegro Financial Markets" international conference
why_relevant: Regulator-hosted annual conference (3rd edition Sept 2025, 520+ participants from 24 countries), co-organised with Ministry of Finance and CBCG. Sponsor list is explicitly published — Visa named platinum sponsor — making it a clean read on which payment schemes and vendors are buying institutional proximity in ME.

source_name: MONSTAT — Statistički biznis registar (SBR) methodology and releases
why_relevant: The Statistical Business Register defines the population of active business entities in ME, classified by KD 2010 (= NACE Rev.2). The methodology document explains how activity codes and activity/size/municipality breakdowns are derived — needed to interpret any 'how many IT/financial firms exist in ME' number correctly.

source_name: MONSTAT — 'Broj i struktura poslovnih subjekata' annual releases (saopštenja)
why_relevant: Annual statistical releases giving counts and structure of active business entities by NACE sector, size and municipality. Quantifies the addressable population of financial-sector and IT/J-sector firms in ME, and the year-on-year series shows sector growth or contraction.

source_name: Payten — Montenegro country/market presence page (Montenegrin Foreign Investors Council member profile as corroborating pointer)
why_relevant: Vendor self-description of its Montenegro footprint with quantified installed base: present since 2006, ~28 staff, six service centres, >500 ATMs and >13,000 POS delivered, >350 ATMs and >7,000 POS currently maintained, long-term partnerships with nine of the country's eleven banks. This is directly competitor-sizing evidence.

source_name: Deloitte CEE/CE banking sector surveys (e.g. CEE banking sector impact surveys, Banking Barometers)
why_relevant: Regional Deloitte CEE banking surveys benchmark digital-channel investment, core-banking modernisation and cost programmes across SEE and typically include Montenegrin banks in the sample; gives comparative competitor context for vendors.

source_name: EPC — Adherence Guide and List of SEPA Scheme Countries (documents)
why_relevant: Records Montenegro's admission to SEPA geographical scope and the operational readiness date — the hard dates that gate bank-side implementation programmes. The Adherence Guide defines the NASO role that shapes who coordinates the national migration.

source_name: IMF eLibrary - Montenegro Staff Country Reports series (structured archive)
why_relevant: Machine-readable/XML rendering of the same Article IV reports, easier to parse and to backfill a multi-year time series of statements about the payment system, bank IT and supervisory modernisation.

source_name: Forum izvršnih direktora (FID) — Montenegro CEO forum, sponsor tiers
why_relevant: Annual Podgorica CEO forum (Hilton) whose sponsor tiers are published by name: Mtel diamond, NLB Banka AD Podgorica platinum alongside EPCG, Lognet, Nu Energy. Direct evidence of which banks are spending on executive-level visibility and which local IT firms sit beside them.

source_name: Zakon o javnim nabavkama Crne Gore (consolidated text) — Paragraf.me / Sluzbeni list CG
why_relevant: The consolidated Public Procurement Act (Sl. list CG 74/19, 3/23, 11/23) defines publication duties, thresholds, procedure types (otvoreni postupak, jednostavna nabavka, direktni sporazum) and the standard forms (Obrazac 1-18). Needed to know what MUST be published — and therefore what absence in CeJN actually means — and to build the document-type taxonomy for parsing.

source_name: Slobodna Evropa / regional media — TIPS-clone instant payments rollout in ME and BiH
why_relevant: Documents the Bank of Italy / TIPS-clone Western Balkans arrangement and the all-11-banks ME go-live — the single largest recent payments-infrastructure change, which drives PSP and bank integration spend.

source_name: Temenos success stories — NLB group
why_relevant: Group-level vendor case study covering NLB across SEE including Montenegro; establishes group-standard platform decisions that cascade to the ME subsidiary even when the ME entity is never named directly.

source_name: BIS central bankers' speeches — Montenegro event speeches mirror
why_relevant: Free, permanent, machine-readable mirror of CBCG governor speeches delivered AT conferences, including the venue, co-organisers and audience composition. Useful when the ME organiser's own site publishes no agenda.

entity_name: Connecting Region / regional trade press coverage of ME bank launches
source_name: Connecting Region / regional trade press coverage of ME bank launches
why_relevant: Regional business media pick up ME bank launch announcements and often add the partner/vendor detail that the bank's own release omits. Serves as both a corroboration layer for bank claims and a discovery layer for launches whose original press release is no longer online.

source_name: Council of Europe — Analysis of the media sector in Montenegro
why_relevant: A mapped inventory of Montenegrin media with ownership and reach, in sr. This is the meta-source for completing the outlet inventory for this cell and for assessing each outlet's independence and likely PR-capture — directly informing credibility scoring.

source_name: European Commission - Montenegro Report (enlargement package SWD), financial services & digital chapters
why_relevant: Annual EC assessment (SWD(2025) 754 final) grades Montenegro on Chapter 4/9 financial services, payment-services alignment (PSD2), SEPA accession and digitalisation of public/financial services, naming legislative and infrastructure programmes and their timelines - the single most citable IFI-grade description of the modernisation agenda.

source_name: Gecko HRM - Lovćen banka case study
why_relevant: A named, written case study describing how Lovćen banka modernised HR operations and compliance with Gecko HRM. Demonstrates the general pattern for this cell: when a ME bank will not disclose a supplier, the supplier publishes a case study naming the bank. Also extends the actor map beyond core banking into adjacent enterprise software bought by banks.

entity_name: Global vendor customer-success libraries with ME bank entries
source_name: Global vendor customer-success libraries with ME bank entries (e.g. Qualys case study on Crnogorska Komercijalna Banka)
why_relevant: Demonstrates the pattern that ME bank references are published on the vendor's global/EMEA site, not locally. Vendor case-study libraries (security, core banking, cards, ATM) are therefore a primary discovery channel for who supplies Montenegrin banks — usually via a regional Adriatic partner named in the text.

source_name: Klix.ba report — Monri Payments and Glovo card-payment partnership for BiH and Montenegro
why_relevant: Concrete, dated example of a cross-border PSP win covering Montenegro — the kind of announcement that reveals merchant-side contracts otherwise invisible.

source_name: Montenegro Business (monte.business) - English-language sector commentary on banking digitalisation
why_relevant: Secondary aggregator that summarises IMF/EC/CBCG findings on SEPA integration, mobile-banking growth and branch restructuring; useful as an early-warning pointer to the primary adviser/IFI documents rather than as evidence itself.

source_name: Pilot Reform Monitor - Montenegro semester reports (independent reform tracking)
why_relevant: Independent analyst-layer tracking of Montenegro's EU Reform Agenda milestones, including digital and financial-sector measures; useful to date programme slippage that Big-4/IFI documents describe only in general terms.

source_name: PropisiNet.me — Zakon o platnom prometu (consolidated law with amendment history)
why_relevant: Consolidated text showing the amendment chain (62/2013, 6/2014, 111/2022, 7/2023, 15/2025). Each amendment wave is a leading indicator of bank IT/compliance procurement; the dates scope which archived vendor pages to hunt for.

source_name: Prva banka Crne Gore - Elektronsko bankarstvo pages
why_relevant: Oldest ME bank (founded 1901). Its e-banking pages and app describe the digital channel; the Android package id of its app (hr.asseco.android.jimba.prvabanka) independently identifies Asseco as the channel supplier. Bank product pages plus store metadata together give attribution the bank never states in prose.

source_name: Strategija digitalne transformacije Crne Gore 2022–2026 (PDF, MJU)
why_relevant: The state digital-agenda master document: lists planned information systems, e-payment/e-service workstreams, responsible institutions and indicative budgets — i.e. the forward pipeline of state IT and payment integrations that later become named contracts.

source_name: Zbornik radova Pravnog fakulteta UCG — 'Digitalna transformacija javne uprave u Crnoj Gori kroz prizmu EU integracija'
why_relevant: Academic review of Montenegro's public-administration digitalisation with comparative Western Balkans framing; useful for a referenced inventory of programmes and institutions, including ones whose primary pages are gone.

source_name: Ziraat Bank Montenegro - Elektronsko bankarstvo & terms PDFs
why_relevant: The bank's e-banking product pages and the associated 'Opšti uslovi za e-banking' PDF describe the channel, its components and sometimes the third-party service centre behind it. Terms-and-conditions documents are an underrated vendor-reveal channel because they must name the operator of the service.
